clinicalPearls: Caused by variants in FLNC encoding filamin C, an actin-crosslinking protein anchoring the sarcomeric Z-disc and sarcolemma in striated muscle; inheritance is typically autosomal dominant.

Genotype broadly predicts phenotype: dominant-negative/aggregating variants tend to cause myofibrillar myopathy, whereas truncating loss-of-function variants cause arrhythmogenic or dilated cardiomyopathy with high sudden-death risk.
Myofibrillar filaminopathy usually presents in adulthood with slowly progressive proximal and axial weakness, often beginning in the lower limbs and pelvic girdle before upper limbs.
Respiratory muscle weakness can appear relatively early and disproportionate to limb weakness, so surveillance of forced vital capacity is important.
Muscle biopsy shows myofibrillar disintegration with protein aggregates that stain for filamin C, desmin and myotilin, together with rimmed vacuoles.
Cardiac involvement — conduction disease, ventricular arrhythmia, dilated or restrictive/arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy — may occur with or without skeletal myopathy and is a leading cause of death.
A distinct distal myopathy phenotype exists with predominant hand and lower-leg weakness and comparatively preserved cardiac function.
Because truncating FLNC variants carry substantial arrhythmic risk, cardiac evaluation and family cascade screening are essential even when muscle symptoms are mild.
reference.pathophysiology: Filamin C is a large homodimeric protein, expressed almost exclusively in striated muscle, that crosslinks actin filaments and links the sarcomeric Z-disc to the sarcolemma and costameres, contributing to mechanical integrity and mechanosignalling. Missense and small in-frame variants, particularly in the rod and dimerisation domains, tend to produce misfolded protein that aggregates within the myofibril, disrupting the Z-disc and secondarily sequestering desmin and other Z-disc proteins — the hallmark of myofibrillar myopathy with characteristic cytoplasmic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles reflecting impaired autophagic clearance. In contrast, truncating variants that trigger nonsense-mediated decay cause haploinsufficiency, which in the heart predisposes to a dilated or arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with fibrofatty remodelling, conduction disease and ventricular arrhythmia, frequently without prominent skeletal muscle disease. This genotype-phenotype divide explains why some patients present to neuromuscular services with weakness and aggregate pathology while others present to cardiology with arrhythmia or heart failure, and why sudden cardiac death can precede or dominate the clinical picture.
additionalDifferentials: Desminopathy and other myofibrillar myopathies (myotilin, BAG3, ZASP/LDB3, crystallin alpha-B)
Inclusion body myopathy with rimmed vacuoles
Other genetic dilated/arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies (titin, lamin A/C, desmoplakin)
additionalInvestigations: FLNC sequencing within a combined myopathy/cardiomyopathy gene panel with variant-type interpretation
Muscle biopsy with immunostaining for filamin C, desmin and myotilin and light-microscopy for rimmed vacuoles
Muscle MRI to define the pattern of selective muscle involvement
ECG, ambulatory rhythm monitoring and echocardiography for conduction disease and cardiomyopathy
Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement to detect myocardial fibrosis
Respiratory function testing including erect and supine vital capacity
redFlags: Ventricular arrhythmia, syncope or high-grade conduction block indicating sudden-death risk
Truncating FLNC variant identified, mandating urgent cardiac assessment
Falling forced vital capacity or symptoms of nocturnal hypoventilation
Rapidly progressive weakness or new cardiac symptoms
Family history of premature sudden cardiac death
reference.prognosis: Myofibrillar filaminopathy is generally slowly progressive over years, but overall prognosis is dominated by cardiac and respiratory complications; truncating variants confer significant risk of malignant arrhythmia and sudden death. Early cardiac surveillance, defibrillator therapy where indicated and respiratory support improve outcomes.
pitfalls: Assessing skeletal muscle alone and missing life-threatening cardiac disease, especially with truncating variants
Failing to distinguish aggregating from truncating variants when counselling on arrhythmic risk
Attributing aggregate pathology to desminopathy without confirmatory filamin C studies
Neglecting respiratory surveillance in ambulant patients
Not offering cascade screening to relatives at risk of sudden death
